name: Hungary

paths.name: Holding the portfolio personally
paths.note: 15% on dividends and realised gains; no inheritance tax between parents and children.

paths.name: Asset management foundation (vagyonkezelő alapítvány)
paths.note: The foundation owns the portfolio, so nothing passes at the parents' death; the children are beneficiaries. Payouts to them are taxed at 15%.

checks.working: Foreign dividends HUF 200m: 15% personal income tax (Szja tv. §66), less the 15% foreign withholding credited = 0; social contribution tax 13% on dividends not listed on an EEA market, on a base capped at HUF 7,747,200 for 2026 = 1,007,136. Gains HUF 150m x 15% = 22,500,000. Draft wealth tax: 1% of HUF 3bn above the family's HUF 2bn allowance (HUF 1bn per spouse) = 10,000,000. Total 33,507,136.
checks.model_note: The engine leaves out the capped 13% social contribution tax on non-EEA dividends (at most about HUF 1m a year); the tax file mentions it in the dividend summary.

checks.working: Dividends and gains received by an asset management foundation with individual founders and beneficiaries are not taxed. Draft wealth tax on the foundation as a separate taxpayer: 1% of HUF 3bn above its HUF 1bn allowance = 20,000,000. Running costs (audit, board, administration) as recorded in the tax file: HUF 6,000,000. Total 26,000,000.
Inheritance between parents and children (lineal relatives) is exempt from inheritance duty (Itv. §16(1) a).

assumptions: No US tax treaty since 1 January 2024 (the US terminated it): US dividends bear 30% withholding in every path, not 15%. A personal investor credits withholding only up to the 15% Hungarian tax; the foundation cannot credit it at all. The projection counts the full 30% on the US share of foreign dividends.
The wealth tax is the October 2026 draft bill as recorded in the tax file; it is not yet law.
open_questions: The draft wealth tax's start date and whether it reaches foundations as separate taxpayers: follow the bill.
Szocho: confirm the 2026 cap (24 times the minimum wage) each January.
